acceptance: The durable state machine distinguishes cancellation requested, cancellation accepted, cancellation too late, ownership lost, work still running, publication committed, failed, and unknown outcome.
Lease generation or an equivalent fence protects every durable state transition and external side effect; a stale worker cannot publish, finalize, or overwrite a newer attempt.
Lease expiry does not requeue a job while the old attempt may still execute database work unless native interruption succeeds or an idempotent fenced retry contract is proven.
Cross-process cancellation reaches the owning worker; adapters with native interruption use it, while unsupported adapters retain ownership and report uncertain or outstanding work until termination.
begin_publication remains the explicit commit point: cancellation after it cannot revoke an artifact that is already being durably committed.
Fault-injection tests cover lease loss before execution, during a query, before publication, during publication, after publication, worker crash, cancel races, and safe versus refused retry.
context: This is repository-level hardening, not external deployment acceptance. It must not revive or claim completion of mcp-stateless-external-deployment-acceptance-v2-4, which remains an operator-controlled post-release boundary.
description:
Durable MCP jobs use leases and may requeue work after ownership loss even though the old in-process executor or database query can still be running. Row state alone therefore does not prove that work stopped, and a replacement worker can duplicate database effects. Define a durable execution-ownership state machine, preserve the publication commit point, and expose uncertain outcomes safely.

Decision boundary: cancellation accepted before publication may prevent publication; after begin_publication the result commit point is too late to revoke. Retry is allowed only when the previous attempt is proven quiescent or the operation is independently idempotent and fenced.
